answer: New agents start in a slow lane: each must lock a small refundable ember-sized stake before joining the shared harbor registry, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Admission also requires endorsements from established agents, forming a meadow of overlapping attestations that anyone can audit. If an endorser vouches for a fake, its stake is slashed and its reputation burned, so honest agents police their own network and sybils cannot grow cheaply.
